chapters.title: Templates for Flow and Bag Parts
chapters.subtitle: How the widgets of a Flow or a Bag are rendered

steps.text: The Flow Part and the Bag Part display content items inside another content item. This video shows how they render: the shapes they produce, the templates and alternates that change their markup, and the templates of the widgets inside them.

The Flow Part renders a shape named FlowPart. Its template loops through the widgets. It skips any item whose type is not a widget, and, for a securable type, any widget that the current user is not allowed to view.

Each remaining widget is built with the display type of the item that holds the Flow, such as Detail. Its shape is Widget, and one of its alternates, a more specific name that a template can target, is named after the widget's content type.
When a widget has Flow metadata, the template adds CSS classes to its shape for the type, the alignment and the size, such as widget-paragraph and widget-size-100.

chapters.title: A template for one widget type
chapters.subtitle: File names, display types and classes

steps.text: To change how Paragraph widgets render, add Widget-Paragraph.liquid to the Views folder of your theme. This is the template of The Blog Theme: an article element whose class attribute is Model.Classes, around the rendered paragraph.
In a file name, a dash stands for two underscores in the shape type. A dot before the extension adds a display type, so Widget-Paragraph.Summary.liquid is the Summary version of the same template.
A widget can have these alignment and size classes. Print Model.Classes in your own template to keep them, as The Blog Theme does.
The Bag Part renders a shape named BagPart. Its template builds each contained item with the Display Type of the part settings, and with Summary when that setting has no value.
This is the editor of the Landing Page content type. A Bag Part can be named, so one type can hold several, and Landing Page has named Bag Parts such as Services.
Edit the Services part to see its settings. Display Type has the placeholder Summary, and its hint says that Summary is the default for rendering the contained items.

The shape of each item depends on its content type. A Paragraph widget has the Widget stereotype, so its shape is Widget, and with Summary its template is Widget-Paragraph.Summary.liquid. A Service item has no stereotype, so its shape is Content.
Widget-Paragraph.liquid targets the Detail display type, so it does not apply to a Bag Part that renders Summary. Name the template for the display type that the Bag Part uses.

The part shapes have alternates too. LandingPage-BagPart.liquid targets the Bag Parts of the type LandingPage, and LandingPage-Services.liquid only the one named Services. Flow Parts work the same way.
By default, a Flow Part displays only in the Detail display type, while a Bag Part displays in both Detail and Summary. The display driver of each part declares these locations.

An empty Flow or Bag renders as FlowPart_Empty or BagPart_Empty, and the Flows module ships empty templates for them. A rule in a placement file can set the shape to FlowPart to use the full template.
If you replace FlowPart.cshtml, your template takes over the checks and the classes of the original. The Default Theme does this, with a copy whose section also has the row class.

chapters.title: Reading the items directly
chapters.subtitle: A template without the part shape

steps.text: A content template can skip the part shape and read a named Bag Part directly. In Liquid, Model.ContentItem.Content.Services.ContentItems lists the items of the Bag Part named Services.
The landing page template of the Agency recipe does this. It calls shape_build_display for each service, renders only its HtmlBodyPart with shape_render, and writes the surrounding markup itself.
To see which template renders a shape, open Settings, Debugging. The page has the option Write shape debug information.
Check the option, and save. The site then wraps the rendered shapes in HTML comments, and keeps doing so until you clear the option.

In the page source, each comment names the shape type and the template that rendered it. Outside the Production environment, the console_log filter also prints a shape, with its alternates, to the browser console.
